\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.embed_rerank_included\endcsname{No. Embedding and rerank requests per question are the counts recorded in preds.jsonl (embed\_req, rerank\_req); they count live HTTP requests only (a vector served from the local embedding cache is not counted), so the embedding count differs between arms for reasons unrelated to the method and is a lower bound of what a cold run issues; they are not priced in cny\_q because (i) their per-token prices in exp/prices.yaml are unverified placeholders and (ii) the tokens of these requests are not recorded per item (usage rows exist only for live requests). cny\_emb\_placeholder is therefore not computable (n/a).}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_27b_fixed.dominates\endcsname{yes at point estimates (single call cheaper without the discount and EX not lower; EX interval as in RV2.pareto.claim)}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_27b_gated.dominates\endcsname{no: without the discount the pipeline is cheaper than the single call (cost 0.0039 vs 0.0060 CNY per question) and EX 0.664 vs 0.671}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_flash_fixed.dominates\endcsname{no: without the discount the pipeline is cheaper than the single call (cost 0.0026 vs 0.0060 CNY per question) and EX 0.645 vs 0.671}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_flash_gated.dominates\endcsname{no: without the discount the pipeline is cheaper than the single call (cost 0.0011 vs 0.0060 CNY per question) and EX 0.639 vs 0.671}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_plus_fixed.dominates\endcsname{no (cost 0.0060 vs 0.0207, EX 0.671 vs 0.679)}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.claim.plus_zs_vs_plus_gated.dominates\endcsname{no (cost 0.0060 vs 0.0108, EX 0.671 vs 0.678)}
\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.cost.nodisc.def\endcsname{disc = CNY per question with the cache discount as in RV2 (tokens that the API reported as cached are priced at 0.2 of the input price, the 0.2 is an assumption of exp/prices.yaml); nodisc = every prompt token at the full input price. ratio.<b>.<cfg>.vs\_<ref>.<mode> = cost of (backbone b, configuration cfg) divided by the cost of the reference, same questions, ratio of sums with the database-clustered interval (.ci) and the item interval (.item\_ci); refs: plus\_zs = qwen3.7-plus single call, plus\_gated = qwen3.7-plus gated loop, self\_zs = the same backbone's single call. Per-item costs are rebuilt from the token fields of preds.jsonl (as the RV2 Pareto claims); route.* use the totals of the usage logs (as RV2.cost.*). front.* = Pareto front on point estimates (cost per question against EX). route.per\_correct = CNY per correct answer: for route\_ca60 the run's cost per question divided by the correct answers per question asked at 60 \% coverage; for the other arms cost divided by EX.}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.gate.hh.def\endcsname{helped (b) = the loop turned a wrong answer right, hurt (c) = right to wrong, paired on the same questions; net = (b - c) / n in percentage points. BIRD dev: 'in' = final minus the root candidate of the same run, 'btw' = final minus the separate root-only run (the keys of RV2.loop.*, repeated here). Spider-Realistic: final minus the root-only run, test-suite EX (the root candidate of a run has no test-suite score). p\_two = exact two-sided sign test (binomial, p = 1/2, on the b + c discordant questions; identical to the exact McNemar test), p\_one = exact one-sided p that helped exceeds hurt. A sign test treats the discordant questions as independent; it ignores the database clusters.}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.margin.def\endcsname{Ratio = 1.5 pp / (loop effect), effect = final minus root candidate of the same run ('in') or final minus the separate root-only run ('btw'), 'fixed' = fixed loop, 'gated' = gated loop, pooled = mean of the three backbones. Each interval of the effect is mapped through x -> 1.5 / x (monotone while the effect is positive); when the effect interval reaches 0 the upper end is unbounded and the text says so. Intervals: cl = database-clustered percentile bootstrap, item = item bootstrap, t = cluster-robust t(G-1), sf = exact sign-flip inversion, wide = hull of these four. A wide interval that contains 1 means the data do not say whether the margin is larger or smaller than the effect it protects. margin.sens.*: P1' EX difference (gated minus fixed, pooled) against a margin of half the pooled fixed-loop effect ('half\_eff') and against 0.5 pp ('abs05'): lo\_* = lower end of the interval of that type, met\_* = lo > -margin.}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.roots.cause\endcsname{Two mechanisms, stated as found (no re-run). (1) Plus: the root SQL text is the same cache replay in both runs; a statement that finished in the fixed run's evaluation exceeded the execution time limit in the gated run's evaluation (status timeout); the gated loop treats a timeout as a failing root and revises, the fixed loop saw a result. Plus: gated 23 vs fixed 18 failing roots, 5 items differ, 5 of them with identical SQL; execution time depends on machine load, so this part is not reproducible to the item. (2) Flash and 27b: the gated run issued live generation requests whose request keys are absent from the fixed run (the prompt of the root request was not identical to the fixed run's; why it differed is not determined by the stored fields, a candidate is non-deterministic rerank output), so the root SQL was regenerated and differs in some items. Per backbone: plus: 5 items fail in only one run (gated only 5, fixed only 0); of these 5 have an identical root SQL text and 0 a different one; 5 involve a root with status timeout; status pairs that differ: timeout vs ok\_nonempty: 5; gated run: 6 of 1534 generation requests were live (not cache replays), 0 of those have a request key that also occurs in the fixed run (a true cache miss); root exemplar lists differ in 4 items, context token counts in 0 items, root SQL text in 2 items (0 of them by whitespace only) | flash: 6 items fail in only one run (gated only 4, fixed only 2); of these 0 have an identical root SQL text and 6 a different one; 0 involve a root with status timeout; status pairs that differ: err\_identifier vs ok\_empty: 2; err\_identifier vs ok\_nonempty: 1; err\_syntax vs ok\_empty: 1; ok\_nonempty vs err\_identifier: 2; gated run: 48 of 1534 generation requests were live (not cache replays), 0 of those have a request key that also occurs in the fixed run (a true cache miss); root exemplar lists differ in 31 items, context token counts in 2 items, root SQL text in 29 items (4 of them by whitespace only) | 27b: 1 items fail in only one run (gated only 0, fixed only 1); of these 0 have an identical root SQL text and 1 a different one; 0 involve a root with status timeout; status pairs that differ: ok\_nonempty vs err\_syntax: 1; gated run: 53 of 1534 generation requests were live (not cache replays), 0 of those have a request key that also occurs in the fixed run (a true cache miss); root exemplar lists differ in 30 items, context token counts in 3 items, root SQL text in 12 items (1 of them by whitespace only)}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.small.def\endcsname{Small-cluster readings (post hoc, robustness). est = headline estimate (item-pooled mean; for ratios, AUROC differences and P5' the statistic itself). t\_ci = estimate +- t(G-1, 0.975) x SE with the cluster-robust SE  sqrt(G/(G-1) sum\_g (sum\_\{i in g\}(d\_i - mean))\textasciicircum{}2)/n  (G = 11 or 19 databases); tdb\_ci = t(G-1) interval of the unweighted mean of the database-level mean differences; sf\_ci / sfu\_ci = \{theta0 : exact two-sided sign-flip p > 0.05\} over the G database-level mean differences with weights n\_g/n (sf) or 1/G (sfu), all 2\textasciicircum{}G sign patterns enumerated; for statistics that are not item means (ratios of sums, AUROC and AURC differences, P5') t and sign-flip use delete-one-database jackknife pseudo-values (tdb = t, sfu = sf). cl\_ci and item\_ci are the intervals of RV2.dual (database-clustered percentile and item bootstrap, B = 10 000); wide\_ci = hull(cl, item, t, sf), wideu\_ci = hull of all six, old\_ci = hull(cl, item). class\_* = reading word under the rule of the contrast (RV2.dual.<id>.rule) applied to that interval; reading\_changes = yes when the word of wide\_ci differs from that of old\_ci (reading\_changes\_u: wideu\_ci). p\_* = two-sided p for H0: theta = null (0, the margin -1.5 for NI(1.5), 0.80 or 1 for the ratio rules). Smallest attainable two-sided sign-flip p: 2\textasciicircum{}(1-G) = 0.00098 (G = 11), 0.0000038 (G = 19).}

\expandafter\gdef\csname xresv@RV2.small.pstar.def\endcsname{Family P* (Holm over P1', W1, P3, P5', m = 4, one-sided p doubled, SAP 15.3) re-tested with the database as the unit: p\_sf1 = exact one-sided sign-flip p over the 11 database-level values (weights n\_g/n, the headline estimand; p\_sfu1 with equal weights), p\_t1 = one-sided cluster-robust t(10) p; P1' EX end point against -1.5 pp, P1' calls ratio against 0.80, W1 and P3 against 0; the ratio and the AUROC difference use delete-one-database jackknife pseudo-values. P1' needs both end points (maximum). P5' keeps its exact McNemar p (not a cluster test). holds\_sf and holds\_t = Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the hull of cl, item, t, sf satisfies the rule; holds\_sfu = the same with the equal-weight sign-flip p and the hull of all six intervals. The smallest attainable one-sided p is 2\textasciicircum{}-11 = 0.00049 (0.00098 doubled), against 0.0001 for the percentile bootstrap.}
